But, especially as a style writer, half the fun of the holidays is having a good excuse to put together a good outfit.

My family’s Thanksgiving gatherings tend to be pretty casual, so I’m not one to show up in anything overly dressy or uncomfortable. I’m usually somewhere in the middle, opting for an outfit that looks like I made an effort but still lets me enjoy a second helping of stuffing without worrying about a too-tight waistband. Think a great sweater with loose-fitting jeans, a knit dress with boots, or even a smartly-styled leggings outfit. Because as much as I love dressing up for the holidays, I also want to enjoy post-dinner card games or sit comfortably on the couch afterward.

It has been revealed that if you’re approaching Thanksgiving dressing the same way, I’ve rounded up six outfit ideas to help get you inspired. I’ve included a few options perfect for a Christmas card photoshoot, along with more laid-back looks that are just as fitting for a casual family gathering. No matter what your holiday plans look like, these outfits strike that happy medium between looking good and feeling comfortable. Now, if you’ll excuse me, I have some mac and cheese to make.

In my opinion, there’s no outfit more perfect for the holidays than a sweater dress and boots. It’s cute enough for family photos but loose and soft enough to keep you comfy all day (especially if you kick the boots off at the door). Grab a long-sleeve knit dress that hits somewhere between mid-thigh and the knee and pair it with some fleece-lined tights and your fave knee-high boot. A midi or maxi dress with an ankle bootie works too.

Express Mock Neck Mini Sweater Dress.

Sam Edelman Sylvia Knee-High Boot.

Start by pulling out a denim jacket and denim skirt. From there, add a plain white T-shirt. I love brown for the fall, so I wore my version of this outfit with brown boots and a matching brown belt and bag. I love this combo because it looks super stylish, but I don’t feel overdressed or uncomfortable when I wear it. Don’t have a denim skirt or jacket? No problem. You can recreate this look with a leather jacket, jeans, or any neutral mini skirt.

Presics Supima Cotton Box Cut T-Shirt.

This outfit has been one of my go-tos lately because it’s so comfortable, but the monochrome palette and shiny finish of the pants make it look like I tried way harder than I actually did. You can even make it feel a little dressier by swapping the flats for a pair of pointed-toe ankle boots.

It doesn’t get comfier than leggings and slippers. For ultra-casual gatherings when you just want to focus on family and food without looking frumpy, just style yours a little smarter. Go for a pair of leggings with minimal seaming (especially a pair without a front seam), which makes them look sleeker. Then grab a dressy-looking oversized sweater—something with a boxy cut, a turtleneck, or a nice knit. I find that my tweed stitch J. Crew Rollneck Sweater is perfect for this look. Project Cloud Ankle Platform Boots.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that it’s late Friday afternoon in Manhattan and Alexis Piqueras has misplaced his phone. Not that he’s concerned. Bathed in the light of October’s early setting sun, the Spanish-born producer and founder of AP Studio, settles into a Charlotte Perriand dining chair at his Tribeca apartment. The vibe is calm: a mix of warm hues, rich textures, and timeworn woods. Candles perfume the air. And all around us the faces and limbs of figurative artworks seem to join our conversation. “I’ll find it eventually,” Piqueras notes, unperturbed by his absent device.

A break from our harried digital world was what he was seeking when, not long ago, he set out to buy an apartment downtown, having returned to Newly introduced York after a three-year stint in Los Angeles. “Sometimes I need to hide amid the chaos,” notes Piqueras, who has built a busy career collaborating with brands on the order of Louis Vuitton, Celine, and Loewe. His real-estate ambitions transcended any simple notions of an urban oasis. Yes, he wanted peace and quiet. But he also wanted some untouched architectural grit that felt true to the city, in particular his visions of its post-industrial 1970s waterfront.

Piqueras relaxes in the living area of his Manhattan loft with his dogs, Prince and Bridget; artworks by Wolfgang Tillmans (top) and Giangiacomo Rossetti.

A Harold Ancart painting and Prince preside over the entry.

Charlotte Perriand chairs and a custom sofa face off across an Alvar Aalto prototype cocktail table; floor lamp by Isamu Noguchi and seascape by Paul Thek.

In a recent development, he found that in Tribeca. Its warehouses and sleepy streets also reminded him of his time in Berlin, where he fell in love with club culture. His upcoming loft, located in what had once been a 19th-century caviar factory, retains its original brick walls, timber columns, and wood windows, through which he can view slices of the Hudson River. A previous renovation had made smart use of the 2,500 square feet, carving out a primary suite, guest bedroom, office, powder room and pantry alongside the open cooking/living/dining space. It all just needed to be pared back. “The moment you take away everything, you have all you need,” Piqueras states.

Working with the Brazilian-born furniture and interior designer Pali Xisto Cornelsen, he stripped back what time-stamped interventions had been made over the years. In the kitchen, they updated the existing high-gloss kitchen cabinetry with white-painted fronts and chunky solid-cherry pulls, also installing stainless-steel countertops and a new island, trimmed in wood. The walls were coated in Benjamin Moore’s Simply White, the floorboards refinished, and the windows dressed in linen roman shades. “I was conscious of creating a neutral canvas,” notes Xisto Cornelsen, who removed all the recessed lighting. “You’re gonna feel a certain calm.”.

A David Wojnarowicz artwork hangs above a circa-1960 Knoll console.

The den features a built-in daybed; etchings by David Hockney and photograph by Nan Goldin.

Art introduces faces to that expanse. Working with advisor Joe Sheftel to expand his collection, Piqueras has assembled a sophisticated trove with a focus on works by Queer talents of recent or current memory. Those include photographs by Wolfgang Tillmans, Peter Hujar, and Alvin Baltrop, who documented the pre-AIDS gay revelry of the nearby Hudson River piers. Elsewhere are portraits by Larry Stanton and David Hockney. Some bare bodies, Piqueras admits, have left houseguests blushing. But the intention was never skin for the sake of shock. “It’s a lot about community,” states Sheftel. “The apartment also functions that way, as a fun space for friends and play.” A romantic spirit comes across in still lives (a burning candle by Phoebe Helander) and landscapes ( a Doron Langberg painting of Fire Island Pines). Evident too is Piqueras’s deep love of New York City. “There’s also a narrative of activism—of power and creativity through crisis,” says Sheftel, pointing out works by David Wojnarowicz.

In the dining area, Charlotte Perriand chairs surround a Pierre Chapo table beneath a Paavo Tynell lamp; photograph by Wolfgang Tillmans, still life by Phoebe Helander, and portrait by Larry Stanton.

Displayed above the custom DJ station (aka Piqueras’s little Berlin) are works by Wolfgang Tilmans, Seth Baker, and Issy Wood.

A Doron Langberg painting hangs amidst the kitchen’s reimagined cabinetry; photograph by Wolfgang Tillmans and stools by Alvar Aalto.

The library features a mix of vintage Scandinavian finds, including a Märta Blomstedt lounge chair, Paavo Tynell pendant light, and a desk and side chair by Axel Einar Hjorth. The large-scale photograph is by Wolfgang Tillmans and the shelves display works by Alvin Baltrop, David Wojnarowicz, Jacob Littlejohn, Peter Hujar, and Giangiacomo Rossetti. Resting on the floor is an etching by David Hockney.

A Hunter Reynolds artwork takes pride of place above Piqueras’s bed; speakers by Ojas.

The primary bath retains the building’s original brickwork.

Sources indicate that elsewhere throughout the interiors, they added custom millwork, including the office’s daybed and wall-mounted desk, the living area’s bookshelves, and the dining area’s DJ station, a corner Piqueras calls his little Berlin. Tapered silhouettes and bevels soften edges. “There are all these happy surprises,” states Cornelsen, who referenced design heroes like Le Corbusier, Joaquim Tenreiro, and Jean Prouvé. Vintage furniture adds to that neutral rhapsody, with choice finds by Pierre Chapo, Isamu Noguchi, and Alvar Aalto, whose coffee table prototype anchors the living area. It is joined by a cast of other Scandinavian characters, among them light fixtures by Paavo Tynell, the upholstered Märta Blomstedt lounge chair where Piqueras enjoys his morning tea, and pieces by Axel Einar Hjorth.

Collecting and decorating, Piqueras has found, are not unlike his daily profession. “Renovating an apartment is a kind of production,” he indicates. “My skill is to orchestrate.” But it’s a break from the grind that he now gets to relish at home. “Work is insane. The streets are insane. But then I can come here,” he says. “I put down my phone—and then I don’t think about it.”.

A Paavo Tynell pendant crowns the guest bedroom, which features more custom millwork and displays artworks by Precious Okoyomon (left) and Christopher Culver.

A Wolfgang Tillmans photograph takes the place of the guest bath’s vanity mirror.

A Sol LeWitt artwork rests on the den’s custom desk; photograph by Wolfgang Tillmans and chair by Axel Einar Hjorth.

Fera Fruit Oil Claims It’s Healthier Than Even Avocado Oil. Should You Make the Switch?

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1071 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Menshealth

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that EREWHON, EVERYONE’S FAVORITE love-to-hate overpriced supermarket chain made news recently for switching up their oils.
  • Sources indicate that erewhon isn’t the only company hawking fera fruit oil as a way to further health-ify their vegan buffalo cauliflower and turmeric chicken tenders.
  • Fera fruit oil may sound exotic and healthy (it’s made from fruit?), but as a registered dietitian, I'm not one for assumptions when it comes to food.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that EREWHON, EVERYONE’S FAVORITE love-to-hate overpriced supermarket chain made news recently for switching up their oils. Yes, the certified organic grocer announced that it's no longer using avocado oil to fry its cafe food. Instead, all 15 locations are switching to certified organic fera fruit oil.

Sources indicate that erewhon isn’t the only company hawking fera fruit oil as a way to further health-ify their vegan buffalo cauliflower and turmeric chicken tenders. Since launching in April 2026, the oil is now in more than 800 grocers, restaurants, wellness clubs, and luxury hotels like Mezeh Mediterranean Grill and Wynn Las Vegas.

Fera fruit oil may sound exotic and healthy (it’s made from fruit?), but as a registered dietitian, I'm not one for assumptions when it comes to food. Especially when it coincides with the peak of seed-oil fear-messaging. Keep reading to learn what this latest-to-the-scene frying oil is and if it's really worth the hype.

FERA FRUIT OIL is basically palm oil. The company behind it, Zero Acre Farms, trademarked the name “fera fruit oil” for high oleic palm oil, a type of palm oil that's produced by pressing the fruit of a hybrid palm tree called Oleifera × Guineensis (OxG for short).

The hybrid plant was originally planted by farmers to reduce bud rot, a disease that notoriously destroys palm crops. A happy side effect was that the oil also ended up having higher oleic acid content, the same heart-healthy monounsaturated fat found in avocado and olive oil.

TRADITIONALLY GROWN PALM has a problematic history of deforestation, but according to Zero Acre Farms, fera fruit oil is a perennial crop that requires just 0.3 acres to produce a ton of oil, using 15 to 20 times less land than soybean or canola oil.

Of course, Zero Acre Farms’ website doesn't cite sources for these numbers, so I did my own digging. Independent research suggests traditional palm yields 3.3 tons per hectare, which is impressive compared to soybean, canola, and sunflower, which collectively produce 0.6 tons per hectare. But OxG palm yields about 1 ton less than traditional palm, which means the demonized seed oils use 3 to 4 times more land, not 15 to 20 times. So the claims seem a bit sensationalized at best?

COMPARED WITH REGULAR palm oil, high oleic palm oil—including the trademarked fera fruit oil—offers a significant nutritional upgrade.

Industry observers note that traditional palm oil contains about 50 percent saturated fat, including about 40 percent oleic acid, and 10 percent polyunsaturated fatty acids. OxG, the hybrid that produces fera fruit, contains 50 percent oleic acid, 33 percent saturated fatty acids, and 12 percent polyunsaturated fatty acids.

As a dietitian, I can get behind these improvements, but the benefits don't translate to real-world benefits quite as well.

It has been revealed that the only way you'll eat fera fruit oil is if you're enjoying pre-made food, most likely fried food, from an establishment using it, as it's not at the moment available for consumer purchase. And while food fried in fera fruit oil may be slightly nutritionally better than traditional palm oil (which most establishments in the U.S. aren't using anyway), it's still fried food.

Recent findings suggest that this ratio not only contains less saturated fat, but also helps maintain stability over multiple rounds of deep frying compared to other oils. A study presented at the 21st International Oil Palm Conference found that high oleic palm oil lasted more rounds of frying than palm, sunflower, soy, or canola. Because it has less polyunsaturated fat and more monounsaturated and saturated fat, it resists degradation better. This adds up to cost savings, because the oil can be used multiple times, but there's unlikely much of a health advantage. Deep-frying meat and starchy foods in any oil can create harmful compounds, but the link between reusing oil, oil stability, and human health is less clear.

Unrefined high oleic palm oil is rich in antioxidants, including carotenoids and vitamin E. Fera fruit oil is marketed as clean, neutral-tasting, and expeller-pressed, but it offers no guarantee or information on what antioxidants are in the bottle at use or how much.

Sources indicate that so while this all sounds great on paper, it's hard to tell how it actually translates into real-world benefits. Is it worth the hype? I'd personally like to see tangible evidence that it does before shelling out extra money for it, and that evidence doesn't seem to exist yet.

Prior to October 15, Erewhon used avocado oil in its fryers. So while there's no arguing that Fera fruit oil has a healthier fatty acid profile than regular palm oil, how does it compare to other fruit oils, like avocado and olive oil, in terms of both health and sustainability?

While olive oil has strong evidence supporting its positive effects on human health, especially heart health, clinical research on the health effects of high-oleic palm oil, like Fera fruit oil, is limited. In one study, 160 participants had either 25 mL of high oleic palm oil or 25 mL of extra virgin olive oil daily for three months. Both groups had similar reductions in total cholesterol and LDL-cholesterol. While these results are promising, the study was small, and more clinical trials are needed to confidently say high oleic palm oil is as beneficial as olive oil.

Avocado oil has a favorable fatty acid profile of 71 percent monounsaturated fatty acids, 13 percent polyunsaturated fatty acids, and 16 percent saturated fatty acids. Fera fruit oil has more saturated fat and less monounsaturated fat, but no head-to-head studies have tested their health effects.

Sources indicate that when an elite grocery store like Erewhon switches to a fresh fryer oil, it's easy to assume it's the healthiest choice. But I wouldn't be so quick to jump on board.

After reviewing the research and understanding the food climate we're currently in, where seed oils are viewed as the culprit of all disease and beef tallow is a cure-all, this honestly seems like just another misguided trend. In the context of reality, when you eat an overall healthy and balanced diet, the occasional fried food, whether it's fried in avocado oil, canola oil, or fera fruit oil, will likely have very little impact on your overall health.

Kelsey Kunik, RDN, is a registered dietician and health writer who covers all-things nutrition for Men's Health and Women's Health.

Finding the right method or combination of methods that work for your needs might take a few tries, but I've got you covered with my beauty editor-vetted recommendations. Yes, this is the priciest recommendation, but it's totally worth the splurge. Braun works in just one treatment session and boasts smart features that justify the added cost and our top spot. Wohlner relies on this device every few weeks to remove her self-described "super coarse hair." Since laser hair removal isn't permanent, some hairs will still pop up. However, they grow back slower, which is a major win for Wohlner.

Industry observers note that as for the results, they were solid. Wohlner didn't have to shave her hair for weeks after the first treatment, and three sessions later, her hair regrowth slowed down. Read More: Electrolysis Versus Laser Hair Removal.

Finishing Touch is an underrated brand. I previously included the brand’s electric shaver with a built-in LED ring light to illuminate hairs I wouldn't usually see in my bathroom. However, it’s no longer being sold and cost more than double the price. This slimmer version is the ideal facial hair removal tool for budget-conscious shoppers, and I wish I ordered mine sooner.

I can achieve similar results using razors three times the price. The Flawless device is also so much prettier than boring razors. The rose gold hair remover is rather discreet and looks similar to dermaplaning tool. It features a small head that contours along the curves of my face, while the blade ensures I have the smoothest trim.

This device works great if you have sensitive skin that's easily irritated. It's gentle enough to use daily, and I love keeping mine on hand at the office to check my face before walking into a meeting.

Recent findings suggest that the only caveat is Flawless is a razor, so it cuts hair at the top layer of skin, meaning hair will grow back relatively fast. So, as long as you don't mind regular trims, this is an epic choice.

After two years of on-and-off testing, Flamingo still makes my favorite razor. Its sharp blades that don’t tug or pull at my sensitive skin elevate Flamingo to the top of my shower routine.

Recent findings suggest that the brand suggests replacing the blades every four to six weeks, but each blade lasts me closer to eight weeks, meaning a regular four-pack of blades lasts me approximately 32 weeks (eight months) before becoming dull. Plus, this razor set is comfy to use while shaving down to my ankles. It curves along my kneecaps and pits with ease, and it hasn’t caused any nicks or ingrown hairs along my bikini line.

I’ll continue using Flamingo, and at just $16, you can also enjoy smooth skin which includes the razor, four blades, and a holder that fits neatly in cramped spaces like my New York City shower.

Sources indicate that while I don't mind using a traditional manual razor or dermaplaning, it's worth spending a little extra on this electric device, claims Wohlner. This Philips electric razor has a large head and self-sharpening blade to rapidly remove facial hair. Wohlner's been using this facial hair removal tool for hairs and considers it the most effective method for eliminating stubborn upper lip and chin hairs. "While it's too major to remove hair on my brows, it's awesome for those larger areas of the face when you're short on time and want to look smooth and stubble-free," she says.

Recent findings suggest that many other tools can irritate, especially around the upper lip area, which occasionally turns into bumps. This shaver has a hypoallergenic stainless steel head that doesn’t irritate sensitive skin, promptly removing unwanted hair in a single pass without causing pain or discomfort. This device keeps Wohlner's face smooth, and it always glides over the skin effortlessly without leaving it red and raw. It even comes with a built-in mirror in the cap to touch-up on the go.

Pro tip: The large shaver head does tend to get clogged after a few uses, which can be prevented if you wipe it down with alcohol after every use. Taking care of your device will ensure you get the closest shave and that it lasts for years.

The idea of gliding a sharp razor across my face was initially intimidating, but I haven't scratched myself since using the Dermaflash. Unlike cheaper options with dull blades, the Dermaflash provides the most professional-grade shave I've ever experienced while testing dozens of dermaplaning tools. The sharp blade features proprietary Microfine Edges, which are tiny corrugations that get super close to my face without any discomfort.

Most dermaplaning tools only have simple blades, but Dermaflash features a gentle pulsing technology that further removes peach fuzz and dead skin cells instantly and safely, making it handy for beginners and seasoned dermaplaning consumers alike. My results rival pro treatments without the hassle of going to a spa and without the excessive upkeep cost. This tool easily glides across my face, which would normally be a challenge with cheaper, manual dermaplaning tools. Since using this device, I noticed my face cream sinks in quickly, and my foundation looks even more natural.

Recent findings suggest that I try to use this tool every two weeks to maintain my smooth results, but TBH, I use it monthly, which is better for my wallet. The brand advises swapping out the blade after every use for the smoothest results, so anything to stretch my beauty budget is always a win. FWIW: Even a monthly treatment prevents my makeup from pilling, so this tool will remain a consistent part of my routine.

It has been revealed that sugaring is epic because the paste only sticks to the hair, not the skin. It's far less painful than waxing and easier to apply.

I've previously only done professional sugaring, but the at-home process is the same. After heating the roller in the microwave, I apply the stick directly to the area I want sugared, lay down a strip, and pull it off in the opposite direction of the hair growth. The fabric strips are a little big to use on my face, especially on the chin or upper lip, but I can cut them in half, and they work perfectly.

Most sugaring wax is packaged in a tub that can tip over and cause a huge, sticky mess. Schick comes in a deodorant-like stick that easily rolls onto my skin. I like to warm the stick up in the microwave in 5-second increments until the paste has a honey-like consistency. I also need a light layer of sugaring wax to achieve the same results as other alternatives, meaning my roller can last for a few months.

I initially missed a few hairs, so I had to follow up with a fresh swipe of sugaring paste. With some practice, my technique improved over time, and soon enough, it only took me a few minutes to wax the lower half of my face. At just $13 a wand, this at-home technique is much cheaper than going to a salon where I'd easily pay double the price, and for that alone, I'll continue using this kit.

It has been revealed that this hair removal cream isn't the Nair you grew up on. It's a prescription-strength cream specifically formulated to slow hair growth on the face. The key ingredients include eflornithine (6%), which blocks the enzyme ornithine decarboxylase (ODC) that stimulates hair growth. Each batch is compounded together shortly before shipping, ensuring maximum potency.

I've tried many hair removal creams, which sometimes cause redness and irritation, so I was worried Musely would be a problem. Musely provides instant hair-free results, and I noticed my regrowth is slower and my skin remains smoother with regular use, compared to other creams I’ve tried. It has a light tingling sensation, letting me know the cream is working. Unlike cheaper drugstore alternatives, Musely hasn't irritated my skin. It also doesn't have a super aggressive chemical smell like other alternatives I tested, and that alone is a win in my book.

According to recent reports, the major downside of hair removal creams, including Musely, is that I have to adjust when I use my tretinoin prescription around hair removal days. After Musely hair removal, I typically wait a few days before safely applying my tretinoin cream. Otherwise, I might experience redness, irritation, and over-exfoliate my skin. Musely is a worthwhile product, but I prefer dermaplaning or shaving because I value acne-free skin over a fast-acting, pain-free hair removal process.

According to recent reports, your hair color, skin color, and hair thickness helps determine your best facial hair removal method, says dermatologist Blair Murphy-Rose, MD. Also be real about your pain tolerance and bandwidth because the best method for removing facial hair is the one you'll consistently use to maintain smooth results. Also, think about investing in an electric hair removal device to speed up your primping routine and, of course, stick to your budget. Our suggestions start at just $10.

They are epic when you have dark hair and a fair to medium complexion; particularly those with thick, coarse and unruly dark chin, upper lip, and sideburn hair. "This combination of hair color and skin tone ensures that the hairs alone are absorbing the majority of the laser energy," dermatologist Rachel Nazarian, MD,,, recently told WH.

But if you're a four or deeper on the Fitzpatrick Scale like me, you should skip using at-home laser hair removal devices. "You want to receive the right treatment that does not harm your skin," dermatologist Jeanine Downie, MD, previously told WH.

Sources indicate that they work by slowing hair growth and reducing strand thickness by using highly concentrated light to penetrate hair follicles and inhibit future hair growth. While laser hair removal isn't exactly permanent, it can effectively slow hair growth. While the upfront cost is a tad of a jumpscare, these devices typically contain about 200,000 flashes, which is equivalent to 780 at-home treatments, notes Dr. Nazarian.

This is my go-to hair removal method because of the low upkeep. I can easily go 4-6 weeks between my sessions, but TBH, I'll stretch it to every 8 weeks. It is relatively painful since it involves simultaneously removing dozens of hairs from the root, but it's a quick process and the results last longer than dermaplaning or shaving. I've been waxing for years and find the pain has become quite tolerable. On a scale of 1 to 10, waxing my face and underarms ranges from 2—3 and 4—6 elsewhere on my body, with the most painful spots being the back of my legs and bikini area. Sugaring It is similar to waxing but less painful. I've had some uncomfy waxes that stung my sensitive skin, but sugaring is noticeably milder. Ingredients will vary among brands, but there is almost always a mix of sugar, water, and lemon. The golden paste is molded onto your skin where you'd like to remove hair, and you'll gently remove it with a fast flicking technique like waxing.

These are tried-and-true hair removal tools that are cheap, readily accessible, and provide instant results. Your best bet is to use a razor with a non-slip ergonomic handle to keep your shave steady. I also like razors featuring a lubricating strip to help prevent irritation. Depending on how fast your facial hair regrows, you might need to shave daily or every few days, but they're pain-free. Remember to use shaving cream and gently run the blade in the opposite direction of hair growth. There are also manual and electric razors, but I'll discuss that more in the next section.

They feature surgical blades to remove dead skin cells and peach fuzz from your face. These devices also have long handles and sturdy grips to prevent accidental cuts. Because dermaplaning sloughs off dead skin cells, this hair removal tool provides the smoothest makeup application.

This method helps promote cell turnover and collagen production plus minimizes dark spots and uneven skin texture, dermatologist Azadeh Shirazi, MD, told WH. "When your skin is hairless and buildup-free, it looks super toned and bright," Dr. Shirazi noted.

Since dermaplaning cuts the hairs at the top layer of skin, they'll grow back quicker than laser hair removal or waxing, says Dr. Murphy-Rose. So be ready to use this technique 1-4 times monthly, depending on how fast your hair regrows.

According to recent reports, these creams typically contain ingredients like eflornithine, calcium hydroxide, calcium thioglycolate, sodium hydroxide, and sodium thioglycolate to dissolve keratin bond structures of strands, making them pain-free alternatives to tweezing, waxing, and sugaring. Let the cream sit for a few minutes, then wipe it away to reveal smoother skin. If your skin is super sensitive, you could leave it on for 1-3 minutes and then shave it off in warm water, dermatologist S. Manjula Jegasothy, MD, previously told us. Hair will begin to grow back within a few days, so you're looking at a low-key commitment.

These are best for removing hair from a small area of the face, like your eyebrows, chin, and upper lip. TBH, tweezing has mild to moderate discomfort since you're plucking hairs from the root. On a scale of 1—10, I'd rank the pain level from 4—6. Since I have sensitive eyes that easily water, I stay away from tweezing my brows, but I found plucking a rogue chin hair pretty mild. Upkeep depends on how fast your hair grows back. Some women want to pluck every few days, while others can stretch their tweezing schedule to every few weeks.

Dermaplaning tools and razors are either manual or electric powered by batteries or a USB or USB-C cable.

When you pick electric devices like the Dermaflash, you'll be spending around $200, while manual tools, including hair removal creams and razors are much cheaper. With prices ranging from $150 to $600, epilators and laser hair removal devices are definite investments, but still cost less than a series of professional sessions. Some of these splurge-worthy devices also have smart capabilities like Bluetooth, smartphone app features, and even calendar reminders to remove facial hair.

According to recent reports, ultimately, opt for the electric devices if you want a fast and powerful tool that lasts for years and don't mind the upfront cost. Choose a manual tool if you would rather save the cash for other beauty products, like an LED face mask or a red light therapy device for hair growth.

Keeping the above guidelines in mind—type, cost, and manual versus electric devices—I carefully researched dozens of at-home facial hair removal tools. After settling on 12 contenders, I spent several months testing and I was only truly impressed by a handful of picks. I evaluated their ease of use, how often I needed to remove hair, and how seamless they were to incorporate into my routine. I also consulted dermatologists and associate commerce editor Lily Wohlner, about her no-fail recommendations to share the best facial hair removal methods for women worth using in 2025.

In a recent development, many at-home devices can’t distinguish between darker complexions and dark hair, dermatologist Dr. Nazarian previously told WH. Melanin-rich skin is at a higher risk of their skin absorbing laser hair and burning, noted Dr. Nazarian. My advice: Either opt for a different alternative on this list or book an appointment with your dermatologist for specific guidance on the best laser hair removal treatment plan for you.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, engwe has impressed us repeatedly with its value e-bikes at lower-than-believable prices.
  • The Engwe M20 3.0 is a specs monster and blows away the original version of the bike released in 2023:.
  • It has been revealed that the M20 is fairly easy to assemble.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, engwe has impressed us repeatedly with its value e-bikes at lower-than-believable prices. But lately, the brand is climbing the value chain with impressive e-bikes that aren’t just great value but also pack strong specs and impressive features. The Engwe M20 3.0 is a great example….

The Engwe M20 3.0 is a specs monster and blows away the original version of the bike released in 2023:.

It has been revealed that the M20 is fairly easy to assemble. At just over 100lbs, it is a bit hard to move around, but once assembled, it feels like a pretty impressive piece of machinery. I love the street tires on here instead of pretending to be an off-roader. Dual bright headlights and brake light with turn signals really give this thing some street cred. Adding to the safety roster, Engwe upgraded the quad-piston brakes with sporty red calipers and 202 mm rotors. This is not a value bike. The rear suspension is tight, which is great for 2 riders but might feel stiff out of the box for light riders. The seat is *chef’s kiss* even for 2 riders. Very soft and comfortable but not too soft. It even has a little ‘gas tank’ storage area aft the seat, which is keyed and enough to hold a few sandwiches, some riding gloves, or a small purse.

One gripe: There are 3 sets of keys on here, the aforementioned storage area and one set each for each battery. We’d love to see these things keyed together.

The bike/moped/moto came with a huge 1.2 kW battery (or 2 in our case – unless you have a 80-mile commute, 1 should be plenty) that must be charged individually. But with a 60V 8A charger, each one only takes about 2-3 hours to charge, which is impressive.

I did not expect to like the ride of this thing as much as I did. We can dispense with the pleasantries here; it came set to Class 2 mode with a 20mph top speed and stickers to match; a quick Google search will show you how to open this up to 40mph open mode. I take responsibility for my own actions.

The first thing you’ll notice here is that the motor is whisper-quiet, and with the street tires, there is very little road noise, even at 35mph. The half throttle is plenty responsive, a lot more so than the cadence sensor on the pedals, which are vestigial at best here. Those major brakes are a bit softer than I’d prefer, but given a good squeeze, those 203mm rotors and quad-piston hydraulic brakes are going to stop you, the 100lb bike, and your passenger/cargo fairly quickly.

It has been revealed that my girlfriend and I got pulled over for the first time in my e-biking life as I was picking her up at the coffee shop. The cop was immediately apologetic because “he thought we were kids” and not the 50-year-olds under the helmets he encountered. Then he noticed the pedals and noted that we’re all clear and that what we were on looked like a motorcycle and that a couple of e-moto kids had gotten into accidents recently, one hit by a drunk driver and who is still in a coma. While he was already letting us go, I pointed out the Class 2 sticker on the bike, and he gave me the thumbs-up as we sped off at 30mph. This M20 passed the local police test with flying colors. I can’t guarantee you’ll have the same experience in your jurisdiction.

According to recent reports, most of my gripes on this e-bike are inherent to the form factor. It is heavy at over 100 lbs, but you’d expect that with a 3.3kW motor, 2.4kW of batteries, and room for two. That mentioned, don’t buy this bike if you need to take it up stairs or plan to pedal it without assist. In fact, this isn’t a bikepath bike or a put it on the back of your car bike. And, don’t buy this bike if you like to pedal. It’s too big and fast. This is a 35 mph roads bike. Also 3 sets of keys?

Sources indicate that I did not expect to love this bike as much as I have. It is the perfect train station bike for me, and as a bonus, it is a great way to take my girlfriend to the coffee shop on the weekends. It has fat tires, great suspension, a cushy seat, and strong, smooth acceleration and confidence-inspiring braking. It looks cool enough for the cops to think I’m a kid picking up his girlfriend, and it has so much range that I probably won’t need to charge it monthly. At $1399-$1699 (10% off) depending on battery config, this is less than half the price of some of the pricier and admittedly more stylish Super73 options out there.

I understand that some will fault Engwe for selling a 3.3kW motor e-bike as a class 2 e-bike. But I genuinely feel safer on the road, being able to go at the 35mph speed that cars are going rather than forcing them to go around me. Plus, it isn’t like every single car on the road goes over the speed limit. So why not bikes too?

The Engwe M20 3.0 is over the limit but in all of the best possible ways.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • A few of the most important insights are heart rate variability (HRV), which describes the difference in time between the beats of your heart, and resting heart rate (RHR), which is the number of times your heart pumps while you are awake, relaxed and not moving.
  • In a recent development, understanding your HRV can help you make better workout choices and understand when it's time to recover.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

TRAINING WITHOUT TRACKING is like shooting a basketball without knowing where the hoop is, especially if you have an ultimate goal like running a marathon or increasing your VO2 max. Many people reach a point in their fitness journey where they hit a plateau, and more often than not, that flatline results from not having the right information. So if you're hitting the gym on a regular basis and putting in the work, it can be important to make sure that you are getting all the relevant health insights to make sure you're using your time efficiently.

A few of the most important insights are heart rate variability (HRV), which describes the difference in time between the beats of your heart, and resting heart rate (RHR), which is the number of times your heart pumps while you are awake, relaxed and not moving. Heart rate monitors (HRMs) are the best way to get this data.

In a recent development, understanding your HRV can help you make better workout choices and understand when it's time to recover. Generally speaking, your resting heart rate will become lower as your fitness level increases, indicating more efficient heart function and improved cardiovascular fitness. “Over time (and months of tracking your resting heart rate), you'll notice patterns. Maybe your RHR spikes every weekend, in part because you're out late Saturday nights. Or it's lower on Mondays, because you go to bed earlier on Sundays," indicates MH Fitness Director Ebenezer Samuel, C.S.C.S. "All of this data can help you make smart lifestyle tweaks that aid your overall wellness — and set you up to move, look, and feel your best and most alert, whether you're in the gym or at the office.”.

Industry observers note that with the holidays coming up fast, it’s a good time to add a heart rate monitor to your wish list. It can help you start your Newly introduced Year’s training goals on a data-driven note, and allow you to track your progress over time.

Sources indicate that ready to take your training to the next level? Read on to find the best heart rate monitors for you and what to consider when looking for a HRM.

It has been revealed that we've been raving about Whoop for years, and it's still one of our favorite fitness trackers simply because it collects so much useful data. This stylish and understated device uses PPG sensors to continuously check your heart rate, and can use the data it captures to figure out when your deepest sleep is happening.

Sources indicate that every day it delivers a recovery percentage and suggests the level of activity you should aim for, whether that a five-mile run or a rest day. In the past, the brand stuck with a simple black band, but these days there are more color and style options for anyone wanting to elevate the look of their HRM.

I personally am a fan of the ability to check my insights when I want, without a distractingly bright screen that pulls my attention.

While products like the Whoop band and the Oura Ring are relatively latest on the scene, Garmin has been making wearable fitness trackers for a long time now. This heart rate monitor transmits real-time heart rate data over ANT+ connectivity and Bluetooth, giving you the immediate feedback you need to take your performance to the next level.

It has been revealed that this Garmin comes with a rechargeable battery with a seriously long life (two months). It charges easily using the provided 4-pin charging cable, similar to the ones that come with their watches.

Sources indicate that we were also impressed with how comfortable this strap is to wear, made out of a lightweight nylon weave. For placement, you want to put the sensor in the middle of your ribcage against your skin, not over your clothes, so that it can get the best readings. Once you are done with your run, you will be able to connect it to your smartphone or Garmin watch via Bluetooth, and then pull up your stats from the menu option.

Industry observers note that because this Garmin has Bluetooth, it is also able to connect pretty simply to cardio machines at your gym like treadmills if you want to track your workouts there. If you are a Garmin fan, and want even more functionality and access to the Garmin Connect app, you may want to spring for the Garmin HRM Pro model (about $60 more).

Read More: Best Fitness Trackers, Tested by Us.

This is a subtle and sleek way to monitor your heart rate throughout the day. Most people aren't going to wear a ring like this while lifting weights, which is why we love the Oura Ring to track those important metrics during the 23 hours of the day that you're not at the gym. What's most impressive about the Oura Ring is its small size, and how one small ring can monitor your sleep, steps, and heart rate.

In a recent development, this ring gives you all the information you need to make improvements in your daily health and well-being. For those looking to try a smart ring for the first time, it doesn't get better than Oura, which is why it took the top spot in our best smart rings testing and this head-to-head piece against the Samsung Galaxy Ring.

It has been revealed that read More: The Oura Ring Vs. the Galaxy Ring.

Sources indicate that the Apple Watch is by far one of the most popular smartwatches on the market, and like the Samsung Galaxy Watch 8, it also tracks quite a lot of data, including heart rate. Although not as accurate as the chest bands, the Apple Watch 12 gets the job done well enough for the casual fitness goer.

In addition to heart rate, it also features an SpO2 sensor to monitor blood oxygen level readings, an ECG to test for atrial fibrillation, fitness tracking, sleep monitoring, and all the run-of-the-mill smartwatch features. Our editors have already spent some time with this latest release, and it's fair to say we're suitably impressed.

In a recent development, the Samsung Galaxy Watch 8 is essentially a wearable personal trainer and advisor powered by AI. With built-in pace coaching and a heart rate monitor, you can add and customize your workouts for maximum efficiency, helping you reach your fitness goals in no time. It connects to your smartphone so you can easily take calls, receive texts, or pull up directions with the flick of your wrist.

Sources indicate that the newer design is certainly better looking than previous editions. The integrated Run Coach also impressed some of our editors, guiding those who require additional motivation.

In a recent development, that being noted, despite the fact that the Galaxy Watch 8 supports iOS and iPhone users through its companion app, those users might be better over going for the Apple Watch Ultra 3 for the additional integrations. The heart rate measurements and sleep tracking is where this device really shines, which is perfect for those looking for a new HRM.

Read more: Best Smartwatches, Tested By Us.

While it’s not the latest version, the Pixel Watch 4 from Google is packed with useful features beginners will appreciate. (The Pixel Watch 5 is the newest iteration, but significantly more expensive.) One of our favorites is Active Zone Minutes, which uses your resting heart rate to gauge exercise effort and give you a buzz when it's time to step up the intensity so you can make the most of your workouts. It monitors activity, sleep, and nightly blood oxygen levels, tracking your trends over time to see crucial changes in your overall health.

Industry observers note that this is a great pick for anyone looking to get great health insights from a wrist piece, who also would like a subtly stylish look. Since Google now owns Fitbit, this watch features some of that great Fitbit technology, which means there are a lot of great integrations if you have a Google account. But because of this, the pairing with iOS devices is not optimal. Something to take into consideration if you're an Apple user.

Google also knows how to make app experiences easy on upcoming customers, including older users without a lot of time with technology.

Sources indicate that the biggest determination you need to make before purchasing is what your primary goal is for the heart rate monitor. Competitive triathletes may want to splurge on a top-shelf device that wraps around your chest for the most accurate data. Whereas beginners or more casual customers might opt for a more modest option they can wear throughout the day (like a general fitness tracker) for daily health insights. Perhaps you spend a lot of time on the golf course and want to know how your heart handles hours of walking combined with the stress of trying to make par. Of course, you may be one of those high-performing individuals who uses both.

According to recent reports, beyond finding a device that fits your performance needs, you also need one that fits well on your body. This depends on whether you choose a chest strap, a wristband, or a smart ring. In most cases, the sensors need to be secured tightly against your body to get accurate readings. Take accurate body measurements before ordering offline, and be prepared to return for a different size if you need to (especially with something like a chest strap). If you are looking into smart rings, many of the options, like the Oura Ring we list, will ship out sizing kits for a small fee to get the correct fit.

It has been revealed that great data is useless if you don’t have an easy means of getting it. For devices without screens, make sure you check which smartphones and apps they are compatible with. They will usually connect with your personal devices through Bluetooth. For devices with screens, check images of the user interface to make sure you’ll enjoy it. Of course, the devices we are suggesting here with screens will display all the crucial information you’ll want. But some may have better compatibility with iOS or Android, which you’ll want to consider.

Sources indicate that with the exception of the Apple Watches (Ultra 3 and Series 11) and the Samsung Galaxy Watch 8 (two heart rate monitors that are equal parts smartwatch), the heart rate monitors we tested are all designed to run for days (even weeks) on a single charge. We love a heart rate monitor that needs minimal charging, and we also love one that lasts a long time in non-connected mode. Two heart rate monitors that surprised us when testing battery life include the Garmin HRM-Dual (3.5 years if used for one hour a day) and the Oura Ring (7 days while on).

According to recent reports, being the Fitness and Commerce Editor at Men's Health, it's my job to evaluate the latest and greatest training gear. This includes fitness trackers, and throughout the year, I get the latest designs from the best brands, both new and old. I am also a certified trainer, and my personal training includes a wide range of exercises, from boxing to lifting to sprint work. But this story was a collective effort by several editors, who were enlisted to try different models and types of trackers based on their preferences.

Industry observers note that we tested each tracker for at least two weeks and put it through a range of exercise scenarios, from treadmill sprints to weighted pull-ups to deadlifts. My fellow testers included certified trainers who also happen to be editors at Men's Health, like Samuel. For devices that have been around for several updates, we've used most of them since they hit the market. Our tested selection didn't focus on chasing trends. Instead, our picks of the best fitness trackers provide great value and performance at reasonable price points for the data they provide.

All of these factors went into finding our favorite heart rate monitors.

Shopping for wallpaper is an excellent way to discover just how indecisive you can be. Between painterly florals, graphic stripes, and whimsical prints, narrowing down the options is practically a full-time job. And that's before you get into the textures, finishes, and the peel-and-stick versus traditional wallpaper debate. There's a pattern for just about every room, taste, and level of commitment. Luckily, we've done some of the research for you.

Industry observers note that wallpaper can also do a lot more than cover four walls. A scenic mural can feel more like large-scale art, and built-in bookshelves can get a refresh simply by lining their backs. Even a drawer lined with your favorite print can be a delightful little surprise, not to mention a low-stakes project for a first-time DIYer. Whether you're ready to commit to an entire room or just want to test the waters, these are the wallpaper brands worth adding to your Pinterest board.

According to recent reports, consider these pinstripes a subtle way to showcase your team loyalty. This print suits any number of installation methods, whether you prefer peel-and-stick, pre-pasted rolls, vinyl, or grasscloth. There are even metallic accents you can choose for added glamour.

It has been revealed that A geometric print awakens a space in a jiffy, and these Bauhaus circles are prime for a midcentury modern abode. Picture it surrounding a fireplace mantle or in an entryway. Adding the print to a ceiling is an unexpected move that gives the space a wow factor.

Wayfair doesn’t miss a thing—hidden amongst their enormous catalog of affordable furniture and decor is a considerable collection of wallpaper. Every print and pattern under the sun is represented here, from chevron to toile to florals.

This tile-inspired temporary wallpaper can work as a backsplash for a “blah” kitchen, on the walls surrounding your soaking tub, or as panels on cabinets. The tiles have a crisp look and, honestly, look pretty close to the real deal.

When in doubt, toile it out. Toile patterns are an easy way to introduce elevated detail. Their classic, subtle details keep things simple, but dynamic. Plus, they work in many different spaces—a bedroom (child or adult), a bathroom, a backsplash, or a living room decorated with early Baroque pieces.

In a recent development, serena & Lily offers a small, curated collection of nautical, floral, and patterned designs (many that include natural elements like hydrangeas, palm leaves, and sea shells) for dressing up a nursery or bedroom. The color palettes tend to be soft blues, beiges, and variegated greens that play up to the coastal aesthetic.

Sources indicate that for Wedgwood fans, this antique-style print is a serene surprise. (Just keep in mind that it’s not removable before taking on a full project.) Pro tip: The brand recommends using a wallpaper liner if you’re working with uneven wall surfaces to keep the finished project smooth.

Here’s another understated option with subtle texture, available in pastels like pistachio, sand, and sky. The muted tones make a great backdrop to any design style, lending the whole room a sense of calm.

While browsing for furniture, we stumbled upon Anthropologie’s robust collection of elevated wallpaper designs that span sophisticated florals and chinoiserie, damasks, and truly special geometric patterns. Their knack for hand-block prints, Renaissance revival, and arabesque designs makes them a no-brainer for any room that you want to be an absolute showstopper. Don’t sleep on their wall murals, too.).

Green bedrooms are trending, but if you want to up the ante on the soothing factor, look no further than this dreamy chinoiserie mural with cerulean-feathered songbirds and lemons to give your space a bit of joie de vivre.

It has been revealed that showcasing Southern artist Jordan Connelly's signature painterly style, these repeating seashells are a non-cliché way to bring a coastal feel to your space. Plus, the tonal color palette makes this great for a child's bedroom or bathroom.

For subtle stripes and vintage-inspired botanicals, McGee & Co.’s small-but-mighty wallpaper selection is there to fulfill your elevated farmhouse needs. Designed to perfectly suit her existing selection of furniture and decor, McGee’s wallpaper serves as a statement finishing touch, one you soon wouldn’t be able to envision your hallway or powder room without. You’ll even find her take on antique Morris and Co. florals through her pastel-hued collaboration.

According to recent reports, this moody floral is ideal for crafting a cozy corner in a bedroom or den, especially in the navy colorway. Pair with the matching throw pillows for a pattern-drenching moment.

Sometimes all it takes is a simple stripe to elevate your space. Thanks to its neutral colorway, you can liven it up or tone it down to your heart's content with a blend of upholstery tones, artwork, and decor. Treat it like paint, just with a bit more oomph.

Industry observers note that chasing Paper is our go-to when we want something elevated that has a dash of whimsy. The brand is known for designer collaborations, too. Most recently, Fariha Nasir translated the South Asian art of block printing into wallpaper with floral garlands and tapestry-like designs. All Chasing Paper patterns come in four options: faux grasscloth, performance vinyl, peel-and-stick, and traditional paper. While we checked out samples in all materials, we can vouch for the durability and crisp pattern of peel-and-stick. They also offer tile decals (that happen to work as contact paper to upgrade worn countertops.).

Industry observers note that as far as peel-and-stick wallpapers go, the self-adhesive poly-woven fabric of Chasing Paper is second to none. “I am no stranger to putting up peel-and-stick and the Peonies pattern I used for my home office is on par with luxe wallcoverings for heritage brands,” notes contributor Yelena Alpert. “The paper adhered securely to the wood paneling, but it had no trouble coming up if I had to realign a panel. The best part is that I did not get any air bubbles—it’s a DIY miracle.” While Alpert opted for the bold red-and-grey colorway that reminded her of Diana Vreeland’s crimson interiors, a toned-down gold-and-cream is also available.

For fans of cabana stripes, this design from Chasing Paper agrees with minimalists and maximalists alike. It’s tough to choose between seven colorways (though we are partial to daisy yellow), which are all great for different purposes: mud rooms, nurseries, beachy bathrooms, or a design-forward living room.

In a recent development, the contemporary meets midcentury aesthetic of West Elm seamlessly carries through to their wallpaper collection, which includes fetching grasscloth designs and designer collaborations, like their latest with design studio Pierce & Ward. Patterns are geometric and playful but not kitschy, and work perfectly for accent walls. You can also find a few animal print designs and artsy figure drawings that are suitable for powder rooms.

Sources indicate that add this organic, playful peel-and-stick wallpaper to your wish list. Those who aren’t homeowners will love how easy the cleanup is for removable wallpaper when moving day rolls around. And when it comes to wallpaper motifs, simple is sometimes better—the soothing neutrals and distinct geometric pattern will elevate and simultaneously calm any room or nook.

Let’s say you want something neutral and textured but grasscloth is not your cup of tea. The Piece & Ward Floral Lattice design is a worthy alternative as it gives the wall a 3D moment but won’t compete with furnishings, especially if you’re into warm wooden pieces. Include ceramic pieces in your home decor to give the entire space a layered look.

The celebrated 19th century British designer, William Morris, was a traditionalist devoted to his craft in the midst of the Industrial Revolution. He taught himself block printing techniques to create more than 20 nature-inspired patterns that encapsulate the Arts & Crafts Movement. His design brand Morris & Co. was established in 1861 and has shown no signs of slowing down as contemporary designers continue to incorporate the wallpaper patterns in their projects. Each wallpaper design is batch-printed in the United Kingdom, making it a good practice to order all rolls at the same time to ensure the dye lots are the same.

The Strawberry Thief is one of Morris & Co.’s most popular patterns and was inspired by the birds that would pop into Kelmscott Manor, Morris’s home in Oxfordshire, to steal the berries from the kitchen. “The gravure printed paper has this heirloom quality that makes it feel as if it is directly plucked from the archives,” says contributor Yelena Alpert, who has samples in indigo and crimson colorways. “Each cheeky bird is about the size of my hand, and the foliage has this watercolor quality. It would look amazing above wood paneling, painted or not.”.

According to recent reports, part of the Morris & Co., pattern appeal is that each floral motif is actually on a grid, giving it a certain rhythm. Pimpernel, another favorite, is ornate in the way that the swirls repeat without overwhelming the eye. This design is seen in the Kelmscott House dining room and was chosen by Morris himself. It comes in 16 colorways that span blues, greens, and venture into burgundy.

Recent findings suggest that more than just a place to find scalloped accent chairs and fashion-inspired collaborations (Aimee Song and Carly Cushnie, anyone?), Lulu & Georgia also offers wallpaper. Of course, you can find the likes of Morris & Co. and Scalamandre, but the brand also has their own in-house line. Design stars Sarah Sherman Samuel and Jake Arnold have also lent their talents to this stock with luxe grasscloths and ornate botanicals. Here you’ll find perfect pairings for your velvet bed frame or curved sofa.

Designed by Sarah Sherman Samuel, this intricate print is made more luxe with the addition of a subtle paper weave, adding texture to the linework style drawings.

Polka dots are a playful addition to standard pinstripes, creating a whimsical gateway for those more inclined to traditional styles of design.

Industry observers note that beloved for their quirky paint color names like Disco Nap (a pale acid yellow) and Silver Lake Dad (a stormy blue grey), Backdrop Home also makes patterned wallcoverings that perfectly color-match their hues. Once absorbed into Schumacher’s family of brands, Backdrop also rolled out archival prints, textured sisal, and peel-and-stick wallpaper options. Backdrop Home offers the kind of whimsical designs that you can’t find elsewhere. Swirling snakes and quilt-like geometric prints that instantly liven up any room, and will have you saying, ‘Oh yeah, that’s Backdrop.’.

In a recent development, taken from the archives of fabric brand Schumacher, Backdrop Home’s iteration takes notes from John Groth’s original 1957 fabric. The sketched horses and riders pair perfectly with the aptly named Ghost Ranch, a warm terracotta-esque brown.

According to recent reports, available in both sisal and plainweave, this geometric print becomes more subtle the more square footage you stretch it across. While wholly impactful in tight spaces like a closet or powder room, this print transforms in large scale, becoming almost hypnotic with its various plum tones.

With a stock full of ornate prints and patterns inspired by historic European textiles, Transylvanian brand Mind the Gap has something for every design style. Heritage-style plaids for the sophisticated sit alongside Eastern-influenced Ikats and jungle motifs for the maximalist. There are also plenty of coordinating textiles if you prefer to pattern-drench your space.

Inspired by upholstery textiles, this maximalist stripe gives the look of fabric-covered walls without the need for a specialty installation.

Vibrant and eclectic, this floral tapestry-style wallcovering recalls early Germanic florals and the brand founders’ childhoods in Transylvania.

It has been revealed that york knows wallpaper. The wallcoverings producer has been around for more than 100 years and still dips into the archive to bring back designs from the early 18th century. The Susquehanna Valley, Pennsylvania, factory is the oldest and largest wallcovering producer in the United States. Even if you’re not into heirloom patterns, their designer series includes collections from Magnolia Home, Rifle Paper Co., Missoni, and LoveShackFancy, among many others.

The Italian knitwear company Missoni is now accessible to the more budget-conscious clientele with its new premium peel-and-stick collection (which also includes the iconic zigzags and florals). The Fireworks pattern is almost like a non-dizzying version of the 1990s Magic Eye motif. “I just ordered all three colorways—natural, mauve, and warm grey—to help me decide which one would look best as an accent wall behind my bed,” Alpert states. “Even though it is peel-and-stick, the texture is that of real wallpaper—smooth and velvety!”.

A tonal geometric print adds just enough visual interest without overwhelming the eye. This print was designed by Joanna Gaines and the Magnolia Home team to combine the beauty of an artist's sketch with the structure of a true geometric pattern.

Boutique wallpaper brand Hygge & West are beloved for their colorful takes on botanicals and geometric patterns. With best sellers like the Alpine Garden and Bloom, the brand seems to have expertly mastered the ability to create visually striking designs that never overwhelm your space, no matter how small. Even in a powder room, the motifs draw the eye in just the right way, complementing your space instead of taking it over. However, if you’re a maximalist, there are definitely patterns for you too.

The Arcade print blends Pac-Man-like shapes and transforms them into a repeat that’s not dissimilar from a quilt block.

One of the brand’s best-sellers, Alpine Garden’s colors pop against the black background that adds a bit of moodiness to typically saccharine florals.

Not every home comes with a century's worth of character, but that doesn't mean it can't look the part. Best known for its period-inspired lighting and hardware, Rejuvenation brings that same appreciation for Old-World charm to its wallpaper collection. Think intricate botanicals, heritage-inspired prints, and textural takes on grasscloth and sisal that make even a latest build feel storied.

Recent findings suggest that sisal doesn't have to stay underfoot. This Hoffmann print recreates the natural, woven texture in a peel-and-stick wallpaper, bringing instant warmth and dimension to the room.

The soft blue-and-cream palette keeps the Fencott print's small-scale leaf motif from feeling too busy.

According to recent reports, are you more drawn to the cozy, muted tones of winter or the vibrant colors of summer? At Claret & Key, you can have your favorite season on your walls year-round. The brand offers its wallpaper patterns in four seasonal color palettes, each giving the same design a different personality. And if none feels quite right, you can dip into the brand's extensive color library to create a combination of your own. Designs are also available in traditional, heavy-grade, and removable options.

It has been revealed that romeo's hand-drawn leaves give you the look of a custom mural without having to hire an actual muralist. The trailing foliage gives the walls a sense of movement, making this an especially fitting choice for a reading nook straight out of an English country house.

Recent findings suggest that nellie, on the other hand, brings a little sunshine to the nursery or kid’s room with its vintage-inspired lemon print. The Spring palette reads more neutral, with subdued tones that keep the citrus motif from feeling too playful.

Hang that framed landscape elsewhere—your walls deserve a full view. Crate & Barrel's scenic wallpaper murals turn blank walls into sprawling gardens and leafy landscapes that look as though an artist painted them right onto the surface. Its exclusive wallpaper collection is designed in-house and made in the USA by York Wallcoverings, with plenty of stripes, florals, and textured designs for those who prefer something more understated. If you're having trouble deciding, up to 10 free wallpaper samples should help narrow the field.

There's a reason Jardin has all the charm of a hand-painted landscape—it originally started as one. Painted in watercolor on canvas paper, the tree-lined scene was digitally scanned to preserve every brushstroke and subtle shift in color. The result is a dreamy, softly layered landscape that gives your walls the look of an original watercolor.

Vivaldi puts a wallpaper spin on the classic verdure tapestry. Printed on natural sisal, it even has the texture to play the part.

An Anthropic mathematician notes Claude helped him crack the Riemann hypothesis, a 167-year-old puzzle with a $1 million prize attached.

His claim surfaced Friday, one day after the AI firm’s stock-market debut, and has not yet been independently verified.

“I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Levent Alpöge wrote in a four-page note. He claims the method also resolves the broader Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, which extends the question to other mathematical functions.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Anthropic with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

Alpöge claims he and Claude encoded their argument in Lean, software used to check mathematical proofs step by step. His note links to 14 downloadable parts of the proof archive, but its availability does not amount to acceptance by the mathematical community.

Alpöge says he messaged Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei about a possible announcement “late Sunday night,” November 15. He then consulted company leadership and said there was a constraint to respect, without explaining precisely what it was.

“The precise timing is horrible,” he acknowledged. Alpöge rejected a cynical interpretation of the timing, but did not explicitly say the company’s IPO caused the delay.

Anthropic began trading on Nasdaq Thursday, November 19, after raising $81.34 billion in its offering.

Industry observers note that alpöge figured in September’s AI math wars. OpenAI claimed it had solved the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem as he and NYU mathematician Tristan Buckmaster pursued related fluid-equation work, sparking a credit dispute over research priority.

Industry observers note that openAI followed in October with 722 manuscripts generated by an unreleased model, grouped into 372 families of results. Only 162 included Lean-checked main results, and mathematicians demanded stronger evidence rather than accepting the tech giant’s flood of claims at face value.

According to recent reports, some mathematicians fear a “mathocalypse,” with AI solving coveted problems before researchers can learn from pursuing them. Toronto mathematician Daniel Litt warned that, without adaptation, “there’s just no more math in 50 years.” At an MIT panel this week, Buckmaster argued mathematics still requires human understanding.

In a recent development, first posed by Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis predicts where certain zeros of the Riemann zeta function fall. The question matters because those zeros are linked to the distribution of prime numbers, whose patterns underlie extensive mathematical research.

A proof would be a historic mathematical result, since experts have been trying to solve that for over a century.

Lean can verify that formal deductions obey its rules. Mathematicians still need to reproduce the archive, check the formalized theorem matches the original conjecture, and examine the claimed result before considering it settled.

Anthropic previously reported progress on the zeta function without claiming to solve the full hypothesis. Alpöge’s new assertion goes far beyond that earlier work.

The Clay Mathematics Institute lists the Riemann hypothesis among its Millennium Prize Problems, each carrying a $1 million award. Under the institute’s prize rules, a proposed solution must be published in a qualifying outlet, survive at least two years of scrutiny, and earn general acceptance before the prize can be considered.

Sources indicate that carry-on suitcases are quite bland though. They’re plastic boxes that require you to attach a keychain or bandana just to recognize your own. I considered Rimowa’s iconic carry-ons for a short while until I remembered my tax bracket and came back to reality (if you’re unfamiliar, they’re expensive). More palatable aluminum options from Away and Monos exist, but they miss the mark for me, be it style or features.

A lucky typo while searching Porter Yoshida bags led me to Portar luggage. The brand’s aluminum and polycarbonate/aluminum luggage is sleek, durable, and costs a fifth of a Rimowa cabin bag. I used the Portar Aluminum Carry-On Luggage all summer and it exceeded my expectations, and it’s now seeing me through holiday travel.

Portar’s carry-on is exactly what I was looking for lookswise—an unbranded aluminum suitcase with leather handles. Functionally, it surpassed expectations after trips to Michigan, Chicago, Houston, and Amsterdam.

Recent findings suggest that the aluminum shell has held up to TSA's less-than-careful hands over the past couple of months. Aluminum luggage gathers minor dings and scuffs throughout travel—it’s part of the charm—but the black covers any marks I may have picked up, and I don’t notice any. In a recent development, the leather handles are not only a nice aesthetic touch, but they actually make handling the suitcase much easier. They’re substantial and padded, unlike the flimsy plastic strip you see on a lot of carry-on luggage. It makes hoisting it into the overhead cabin a bit more steady and secure.

The latches are also a huge change for me, as I’m used to hassling with zippers that snag or tear—I will never go back to zippered luggage again. Both the telescopic handle and wheels operate smoothly, so I glide gracefully to my gate.

Sources indicate that technically my fiancée’s Away carry-on has more space based on dimensions, but I swear I can efficiently pack more into my Portar. Maybe it’s the clever pocket configuration or the removable compression straps and divider, but coming back from Amsterdam, we were counting on my Portar to bring back Delft ceramics and other acquisitions. All of which fit despite my over (option!) packing.

My Portar will now accompany me home for the holidays. It will also travel to the Pitztal Valley in Austria, then on to Vienna the week after Thanksgiving. It’s a first-class carry-on in the cabin space above my economy seat. Air travel used to be luxurious, and people would dress up for the occasion of reaching 38,000 feet. The Portar carry-on is bringing back some of that charm and costs me less than $300.

Ivy Shapiro's Manhattan Home is an Artful Ode to Old-School Fresh York

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that describing the allure of her sprawling prewar Manhattan apartment, art adviser Ivy Shapiro returns to one theme again and again.
  • A Joel Shapiro sculpture holds a corner of the dining room beneath a painting by Aubrey Saget.
  • In the living room, a painting by Cecily Brown hangs above a Joel Shapiro table with sculptures by Jonathan Borofsky (left) and Ivy Shapiro’s daughter, Lily Crewdson (right), beside a Southeast Asian sculpture.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that describing the allure of her sprawling prewar Manhattan apartment, art adviser Ivy Shapiro returns to one theme again and again. “It’s old-school,” she insists. “I have this fantasy that I’m living in a different era. I wanted the apartment to capture this nostalgic vision of old-school Latest York elegance.” She had plenty to work with. The bones of the unit—its high ceilings, architectural details, and idiosyncratic layout of generous salons and small, meandering rooms—remained largely intact. Major structural alterations were unnecessary to make the space her own, a home that reflects her singular character while graciously accommodating an extensive collection of art that ranges from Stone Age tools and Southeast Asian antiquities to modern and contemporary works created by friends and family.

A Joel Shapiro sculpture holds a corner of the dining room beneath a painting by Aubrey Saget. Works on paper by Edgar Degas and Bob Thompson surmount the fireplace, which is clad in black encaustic tile by clé.

In the living room, a painting by Cecily Brown hangs above a Joel Shapiro table with sculptures by Jonathan Borofsky (left) and Ivy Shapiro’s daughter, Lily Crewdson (right), beside a Southeast Asian sculpture. A Jasper Johns lithograph hangs at rear. Sculpture in foreground by Tony Smith.

Recent findings suggest that A Jeremy Anderson chandelier from Gallery Fumi crowns the makeup room. On the wall are works on paper by Cecily Brown.

Recent findings suggest that shapiro was born into the New York art world of the 1970s, when the artist and collector community had a far different complexion than that of today, a time before “the art world” meant “the art-fair world.” She is the daughter of the late celebrated sculptor Joel Shapiro and art educator Amy Snider, and the stepdaughter of artist Ellen Phelan. Hers is a life organized around and by art, so it is no surprise that the same would be true of her apartment. Here, art is offered the same sovereignty as the home’s human inhabitants, the freedom to take up space, require concessions, demand attention, and even, occasionally, to trip you up. It doesn’t have to fit in above a sofa or over a mantel, nor does it have to stand for something—taste, wealth, a movement, a generation. She accords each piece the independence to exist on its own terms, to be at home.

“I like hanging art in weird places where people don’t like to hang,” Shapiro says. “It’s not an intellectual exercise. It’s more intuitive.”.

Architect Raffaella Bortoluzzi, Shapiro’s accomplice in the gentle transformation of the home, drew inspiration from her client’s unconventional sensibility. “I love that Ivy decided not to combine the small rooms and try to impose a more contemporary approach on how the spaces flow. We wanted to respect the historic character and maintain the eccentricities,” Bortoluzzi notes. “Our idea was that every room should have its own little story. We focused on light, playful treatments that in no way fight the original architecture.”.

Floating tiled shelves in the kitchen display ceramics by Warren MacKenzie and Shio Kusaka and a small sculpture by Joel Shapiro.

The television room features paintings by Lothar Hempel (left) and Elizabeth Murray (right).

A Joel Shapiro drawing has pride of place in the bedroom of Ivy Shapiro’s son, Walker Crewdson. To the right are a drawing by Sol LeWitt and a Joel Shapiro print.

Sources indicate that the television room, for example, is enrobed in aubergine Venetian plaster. The home office, covered in a crimson plaster, features shelves and drawer fronts finished with a surface treatment of crushed eggshells encased in epoxy. Bortoluzzi goosed the primary bath by sprinkling a handful of Piero Fornasetti tiles among a field of pearlescent, zellige-like ones. In Shapiro’s makeup room, ladylike pink plaster walls are amplified by an antique mirror, custom shoe closets with floral fabric behind the glass case fronts, and a sprightly Jeremy Anderson chandelier. “Ivy is very funny and feminine in her way,” the architect says. “The design speaks to those aspects of her personality.”.

In the dining room, a Jean Arp collage is installed above an antique tansu with Stone Age tools and Joel Shapiro maquettes.

It has been revealed that the last sculpture Joel Shapiro created rests on a table in the primary bedroom. The painting is by Bob Thompson. The sofa is covered in a Rubelli brocade.

Shelves and drawer fronts in the home office are covered in a surface material of crushed eggshells by Nature Squared.

According to recent reports, within the newly refurbished architectural shell, Shapiro deployed her estimable collection of art and objets de vertu with wit and verve. In the living room, the way that Jonathan Borofsky’s bronze Split Head sculpture is balanced by the split-off stone head of an Asian deity feels like a call and response across the ages, as well as a vignette about the endurance of art. They flank a dynamic painting by Shapiro’s friend Cecily Brown like chaperones at an orgy of color and motion. A sculpture by Shapiro’s daughter, Lily Crewdson, joins the Borofsky piece atop a table made by her father, one of many Joel Shapiro sculptures, drawings, and maquettes installed throughout the apartment.

A sculpture by Richard Artschwager is installed above a Joel Shapiro bronze in a hallway.

An Axel Salto sculpture sits beneath an artwork by Ryan Sullivan in the living room.

In the hallway to the primary bedroom, a lyrical vintage Danish wall light of abstracted vines, leaves, and flowers hangs above a signature Carl Andre metal floor sculpture, the ultimate butch/femme pairing. In the bedroom itself, a sculpture that Joel Shapiro made in the hospital during his final days (he died in June of 2025) sits inconspicuously on a small table of his own design. It was the last artwork of his storied career.

“Living with so much of Joel’s art, and all these amazing things he and Ellen collected, connects me to [my dad],” Shapiro muses. “The way the apartment is set up, I feel like my life is completely integrated with the art.”.
